title: A bill to make a technical correction to the ALS Disability Insurance Access Act of 2019.
official_summary:
This bill retroactively eliminates the waiting period for Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) benefits for certain individuals with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). Commonly known as Lou Gehrig's Disease, ALS is a progressive neurodegenerative disease that affects nerve cells in the brain and spinal cord.

Under current law, most SSDI recipients must wait five months after becoming disabled before their benefit payments may begin. The ALS Disability Insurance Access Act of 2019 eliminated the waiting period for individuals with ALS but only covers individuals who apply for benefits after the date of enactment (December 20, 2020). As a result, individuals with ALS who applied for SSDI benefits in the five months before that date are still subject to the waiting period. This bill eliminates the waiting period for those individuals.

summary.headline: This law removes the five-month SSDI waiting period for certain people with ALS who applied for benefits in the months before the 2019 ALS act took effect.
summary.what_it_does: Social Security Disability Insurance usually makes beneficiaries wait five months after becoming disabled before payments start. A 2019 law removed that wait for people with ALS, but only for those who applied on or after December 20, 2020. This bill applies the same removal backward, so people with ALS who applied in the five months before that date no longer have to serve the waiting period. The change is retroactive.

who_it_affects.group: People with ALS who applied for SSDI in the five months before December 20, 2020
who_it_affects.how: They no longer have to wait five months before their disability benefit payments begin.
The agency must recalculate and pay benefits for eligible applicants who were previously subject to the waiting period.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: Signed into law on March 23, 2021, with the change applying retroactively to the December 20, 2020 effective date of the 2019 ALS act.
